name: prose-craft
description: Standalone prose craftsmanship for human-facing documentation — align audience, structure pattern, and style profile in a short interview before drafting (prose-draft), review through editorial lenses including model-voice detection (prose-review), and refine through a multi-model rewrite-and-weave cycle whose woven voice no single model family dominates (prose-refine). No substrate dependency.

interface.shortDescription: Draft, lens-review, and refine human-facing docs
interface.longDescription: Standalone prose craftsmanship for documentation that will be published: prose-draft opens with a short alignment interview modeled on ideate — it states the inferred audience and venue for confirmation, proposes directions combining a structure pattern, a style profile, and an opening move, then pins a six-field doc brief plus a reader-path plan (entry state, question-chain beats, define-before-use map, importance tiers) that may deliberately diverge from the heading tree — style is always a recorded selection, never a silent default; prose-review runs a single-pass review through up to six editorial lenses (four by default — audience, structure, clarity, accuracy — plus voice and accessibility), traces structure against the carried reader path, and checks word choice for model-family voice; prose-refine drives the full multi-model cycle — parallel fresh-context re-writers of different model classes, a weave that prefers the least model-toned version of each section so no single model family dominates, scope that shrinks each round (full rewrite, machine-prose tell hunting, micro-edits), and convergence to publication quality within a 3-round cap.
defaultPrompt: Use prose-craft to draft, lens-review, or refine human-facing documentation such as READMEs, foundation docs, and web articles.
